published_final_diagnosis.label: Spontaneous cervicothoracic spinal epidural hematoma with acute spinal cord compression

source_treatment.description: Emergency neurosurgical decompression and hematoma evacuation

source_disposition.outcome: Discharged after two days; full neurological recovery at follow-up.

key_guideline_decisions.note: See docs/guideline_sources.yaml; applicability and alternative care require clinician review.

distractors: Source describes a stroke mimic, but axial pain and bilateral sphincter/leg deficits localize to spinal cord.
critical_safety_points: Treat evolving paraplegia and sphincter dysfunction as spinal emergency.
Urgent spine MRI and neurosurgical consultation.
Avoid empiric thrombolysis for presumed stroke without localization; anticoagulation may worsen hematoma.
source_uncertainties: Unspecified dose, timing or normal findings were not inferred.
Published management is descriptive and requires separate normative review.
